title: Front Desk Security & Suspicious Behaviour
blurb: Keeping reception welcoming and secure: guest privacy, tailgating, suspicious behaviour and unattended bags.
siteNotes: How a guest's identity is verified at your desk.
Who the duty manager is to alert about suspicious behaviour or unattended items.
Where the key and keycard controls are kept.
legalNotes: Not revealing guest details is also a data protection point (UK GDPR); not quoted on slides.

CHECK: the trainer says keep people away from an unattended bag and report it to a manager. Confirm the venue's own suspicious-item procedure (for example when to call 999 or evacuate) and add it to the site notes.

cards.kicker: Office · Front of House · Management · 10 minutes
cards.title: Front Desk Security & Suspicious Behaviour
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- protect guests' room numbers and details
- spot tailgating and suspicious behaviour
- handle an unattended bag the safe way

cards.title: Welcoming and security-aware
cards.body:
Reception is the front line of our security, often the first place a problem would show itself.

Most people are exactly who they say they are. Staying switched-on protects our guests, our team and our building.

items.title: Welcoming
items.text: Most people are who they say

cards.title: Never reveal who is staying
cards.body:
Never reveal a guest's room number or confirm whether someone is staying with us.

If someone asks to be let into a room or wants a guest's details, verify they are that guest, or have permission, first. Control room keys and keycards carefully.

left.title: Do
items: Verify they are the guest first

right.title: Do not
items: Let someone in because they ask

cards.title: Who came through behind you?
cards.body: Watch for "tailgating": someone slipping through a door into staff-only or guest areas behind you.

items.title: Notice
items.text: Someone follows you through a door

cards.title: Trust your instincts
cards.body:
Be alert to someone loitering, avoiding eye contact or staff, asking unusual questions about security, rooms or guests, or trying doors.

If something feels off, it is worth a second look. Challenge politely, or if you are unsure, quietly alert a manager.

cards.title: Bags and packages
cards.body:
Do not touch or move an unattended bag or package. Keep people away and report to a manager, who will decide what to do.

A friendly, observant front desk keeps the whole venue safer without ever feeling unwelcoming.

items.title: Do not touch
items.text: Do not open or move it

items.title: Report
items.text: A manager decides what to do

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Never reveal a room number or confirm who is staying.
- Verify a person is the guest, or has permission, before letting them into a room.
- Control room keys and keycards carefully.
- Trust your instincts: challenge politely or alert a manager.
- Do not touch an unattended bag. Keep people away and report it.

cards.q: You should never reveal a guest's room number.
cards.why: Never reveal a guest's room number or confirm whether someone is staying with us.

cards.q: Before letting someone into a room, what must you do?
options: Ask them to say the room number
Judge whether they look the part
Verify they are that guest, or have permission
Take their word if they are polite to you
cards.why: Verify they are that guest, or have permission, first.

options: Following a car too closely on the road
Someone slipping through a door behind you
A guest queuing at reception desk
Walking a guest through to their room
cards.why: Tailgating is someone slipping through a door into staff-only or guest areas behind you.

cards.q: If something feels off about a person, it is worth a second look.
cards.why: Trust your instincts. If something feels off, it is worth a second look.

cards.q: Which of these is a sign of suspicious behaviour at reception?
options: Asking where the bar is
Waiting for a lift
Reading the menu
Trying doors
cards.why: Loitering, avoiding staff, unusual questions about security or guests, and trying doors are signs.

options: Left alone, kept clear and reported
Opened to find the owner
Moved to lost property
Carried to the manager's office
cards.why: Do not touch or move it. Keep people away and report it to a manager.

cards.q: You should confirm to a caller whether a named person is staying with us.
cards.why: Never confirm whether someone is staying with us.

cards.q: Being welcoming and being security-aware can go together.
cards.why: Being welcoming and being security-aware go hand in hand.

cards.q: A polite way to check on someone unfamiliar in a staff area is…
options: Ignore them and carry on
"Can I help you find something?"
Tell them to leave at once
Follow them without a word
cards.why: You can challenge politely with "Can I help you find something?" or quietly alert a manager.

cards.q: Room keys and keycards should be controlled carefully.
cards.why: Control room keys and keycards carefully.
